primary_sources.title: The numeraire e-variable and reverse information projection
primary_sources.relevant_scope: Sections 2, 4 and 7; point alternative versus composite null, common-reference universal-inference comparison

primary_sources.title: Safe testing
primary_sources.relevant_scope: Definition 1 and Proposition 2 on conditional e-variables and optional continuation

verified_observations: Larsson-Ramdas-Ruf define the numeraire X* for a point alternative against a composite null and establish its log-optimality among e-variables.

In Section 7, under a common reference measure, universal inference is X_UI=q/p_max while the numeraire is X*=q/p*. Their Lemma 7.1 yields p*<=p_max almost everywhere, hence X*>=X_UI pointwise almost everywhere; nondegenerate composite-null cases generally have strict inequality on positive measure.

The same paper explicitly lists extending the numeraire theory to the sequential setting using nonnegative supermartingales/e-processes as future work. Therefore its static theorem alone is not a sequential-validity theorem.

Safe Testing Definition 1 and Proposition 2 separately show that a sequence of filtration-conditional e-variables has a running-product test supermartingale and remains valid under optional continuation/stopping at the study level. Conditional e-values may be constructed just in time from past information if the conditional e-validity requirement is satisfied.

scope_refinement.supported: For each frozen-reference block, if the induced q_R versus composite null P_R problem has a correctly certified numeraire factor under a common reference measure, the static factor is pointwise no smaller than the corresponding universal-inference factor for that same block.
scope_refinement.sequential_bridge: Multiplying such block factors is sequentially safe only after proving that each chosen block factor is an F_{m-1}-conditional e-variable for the actual filtration/null. Safe Testing supplies the composition theorem; the numeraire paper does not by itself supply this conditional/sequential step.
scope_refinement.four_corner_candidate: The proposed four-corner p_rho has not yet been certified to satisfy the full continuum constraint and therefore is not yet established as the RIPr/numeraire. Pointwise dominance over universal inference cannot be promoted from the exact-numeraire theorem to this numerical candidate until e-validity/RIPr certification is complete.
scope_refinement.architecture_claim: The assertion that the replacement factor preserves the worker's O(1) delayed-start telescoping recursion is an implementation/architecture claim, not a result supplied by either cited statistics paper; it was not independently replayed in this audit.

not_verified_here: The reported four-corner mixture weight rho≈0.55441744 and +1.04289 nat/block numerical gain were not independently recomputed.
The r85/r84/r82 detector latency tables were not independently rerun.
No continuum interval proof of C(mu,sigma)<=1 was found or inferred.
exact_tested_scope: Primary-source theorem/proposition audit only; no worker simulation or detector code replay.
